Axiom NHI’s Inline Rust Data Plane Is Production-Grade, but 10 Control-Plane Wiring and Security Gaps Block Final Launch

Forensic source-code reconciliation of GurnoorBagga17/New (commit faa1715, evaluated November 17, 2026) against the 22 architectural specifications in complete-audit.zip reveals a sharp divide: the sub-2ms inline ExtMCP gRPC runtime is real and functional, whereas six enterprise Rust crates remain disconnected from the HTTP control plane and return static JSON mocks.

Your inline runtime wedge—the hardest systems engineering challenge in an AI agent security gateway—is genuinely built. In services/extmcp/runtime/src/main.rs, the Tonic gRPC server (:9001), official AWS cedar_policy v4 engine with lock-free ArcSwap hot-reload, sqlparser-rs AST destructive DDL trap, path canonicalizer, DNS-pinned SSRF firewall, RFC 8785 JCS tool schema pinning, and SHA-256 Merkle-chained JSONL audit bus all execute real logic. Furthermore, the underlying enterprise crates (lineage-graph/src/postgres.rs, secretless/src/openbao.rs, fleet-control/src/spicedb.rs, and connectors/src/discovery.rs) contain real sqlx and reqwest client implementations.

However, complete-audit.zip overstates end-to-end completion by treating isolated crate code as wired production functionality. When main.rs boots, it connects to PostgreSQL, runs 0001_phase2_graph.sql, and immediately drops the PostgresLineageGraph connection pool at the end of the if block. Consequently, services/extmcp/runtime/src/admin.rs still serves hard-coded demo JSON for /v1/lineage/graph, /v1/secretless/leases, /v1/secretless/rotate, and /v1/owasp/scorecard, while accepting a hard-coded backdoor bearer token (axm_local_dev_token_for_browser_testing) across wildcard CORS.

Audit Zip Claims vs. Live Repository Reality

In IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md inside complete-audit.zip, 16 of 22 capabilities (73%) are scored as COMPLETE and 0% of the repo is marked broken. Cross-examining the actual handlers in admin.rs and GitHub Actions Run #16 shows that six of those "Complete" capabilities are implemented as standalone library crates that are never instantiated or called by the running binary.

Closing this "last-mile wiring gap" between your Rust workspace crates and AdminApiState is the single highest-leverage engineering task between your current codebase and a customer-ready production deployment.

Master Register of 10 Production & Deployment Gaps

Every gap below was verified directly against the main branch of GurnoorBagga17/New. P0 blockers represent immediate security vulnerabilities, dropped database connections, or failing CI pipelines that prevent cutting a production release; P1 gaps break multi-instance cloud or browser deployments; P2 gaps cover workload attestation hardening and public repo hygiene.

GAP-01 · P0 Admin API Auth & CORS
services/extmcp/runtime/src/admin.rs 		SECURITY_AUDIT.md claims loopback auth is enforced in prod. In reality, require_admin_token unconditionally accepts the hard-coded bearer string "axm_local_dev_token_for_browser_testing" and pairs it with CorsLayer::new().allow_origin(Any), allowing any malicious site visited by an operator to hot-swap Cedar rules or trigger revocations on 127.0.0.1:8787. Gate the fallback dev token strictly behind AXIOM_DEV_MODE == "1", require AXIOM_ADMIN_TOKEN (≥32 bytes) in production, and restrict CORS to explicit origins in AXIOM_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.
GAP-02 · P0 PostgreSQL Pool Dropped
services/extmcp/runtime/src/main.rs 		IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md marks PostgreSQL 16 Lineage Graph COMPLETE. In main.rs, PostgresLineageGraph::connect(&db_url) runs migrations and then goes out of scope and is dropped. AdminApiState only holds the in-memory engine, and GET /v1/lineage/graph ignores _engine to return 5 static JSON nodes. Store Option<Arc<PostgresLineageGraph>> inside AdminApiState and wire /v1/lineage/graph and /v1/lineage/simulate-revoke to query PostgreSQL when configured.
GAP-03 · P0 Multi-Tenant RLS Bypass
lineage-graph/src/postgres.rs 		DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md claims 0002_tenant_rls.sql is embedded and enforced. Add include_str!("../migrations/0002_tenant_rls.sql") to run_migrations(), add FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, and call set_config('app.current_tenant', $1, true) per transaction.

Deep Dive 1: Unwiring in the Rust Admin Engine (services/extmcp/runtime)

The most important insight from auditing GurnoorBagga17/New is that your Rust workspace crates are not empty stubs—they contain real SQL queries, HTTP clients, and cryptographic math that simply stop one step short of being connected to services/extmcp/runtime/src/admin.rs.

1. Dropped PostgresLineageGraph

In services/extmcp/runtime/src/main.rs, startup checks std::env::var("DATABASE_URL"), calls PostgresLineageGraph::connect(&database_url).await, runs postgres_graph.run_migrations().await, and exits the block—dropping the PgPool immediately. Meanwhile, admin::create_seeded_lineage_engine() populates an in-memory graph, and get_lineage_graph in admin.rs binds _engine with an underscore and returns a hard-coded JSON literal.

2. Offline Secretless & SpiceDB

secretless/src/openbao.rs defines a real OpenBaoClient that sends GET {base_url}/v1/{mount}/creds/{role} with X-Vault-Token, and fleet-control/src/spicedb.rs defines a real SpiceDbClient calling /v1/permissions/checkPermission. Yet admin.rs never imports either struct: attest_and_lease calls the offline helper issue_attested_openbao_lease against two static SHA-256 digests.

3. Feature-Gated Cloud Connectors

In connectors/src/discovery.rs, AwsIamDiscoveryWorker (#[cfg(feature = "aws")]) and K8sDiscoveryWorker (#[cfg(feature = "k8s")]) implement real AWS SDK and kube-rs calls, and SlackDiscoveryWorker calls https://slack.com/api/auth.test. None of these workers are exposed via a POST /v1/discovery/sync endpoint in admin.rs to feed nhi_nodes and risk-engine.

Deep Dive 2: Multi-Tenant RLS & Database Isolation

In complete-audit/DATABASE_ARCHITECTURE.md, multi-tenant Row-Level Security (RLS) is described as complete via lineage-graph/migrations/0002_tenant_rls.sql. Inspecting lineage-graph/src/postgres.rs alongside deployments/docker/docker-compose.yml exposes three concrete defects that leave shared PostgreSQL deployments unisolated:

  1. Migration 0002_tenant_rls.sql Is Never Executed: In lineage-graph/src/postgres.rs, run_migrations() only embeds and runs 0001_phase2_graph.sql. Likewise, docker-compose.yml only volume-mounts 0001_phase2_graph.sql into /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/.
  2. Table Owner Bypasses RLS Without FORCE: Even when 0002_tenant_rls.sql runs ALTER TABLE nhi_nodes ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;, PostgreSQL exempts the table owner (POSTGRES_USER: axiom) from RLS policies unless ALTER TABLE nhi_nodes FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; (and the same on nhi_edges) is explicitly declared.
  3. Missing Session Variable Binding: The RLS policy checks tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant', true), but none of the SQL queries in postgres.rs (upsert_node, upsert_edge, simulate_revocation) begin a transaction that executes SELECT set_config('app.current_tenant', $1, true) using the authenticated tenant ID.

Deep Dive 3: Frontend Auth, 127.0.0.1 Lock-In & CI Gates

Your Next.js 15 application (apps/web) is visually cohesive and implements all 22 page routes and 10 API routes. To deploy apps/web to Vercel or Kubernetes alongside the Rust runtime, three frontend/CI gaps must be resolved:

  1. Eliminate Browser Calls to http://127.0.0.1:8787: Whereas app/api/playground/evaluate/route.ts properly proxies requests server-side via process.env.AXIOM_ADMIN_API_URL, app/console/page.tsx calls http://127.0.0.1:8787 directly from client JavaScript. Create /api/console/events, /api/console/scorecard, and /api/console/revocations proxy routes so browser clients never talk directly to loopback ports.
  2. Harden Session Verification & Remove Silent Demo Fallback: Update apps/web/middleware.ts to verify an HMAC-SHA256 / JWE token rather than checking Boolean(sessionCookie?.value), unify the cookie name (axiom_session vs axm_session), and stop app/console/page.tsx from silently fabricating evaluator@security-team.corp when unauthenticated in production.
  3. Fix Commit faa1715 CI Gate Failures: In Workflow Run #16, check_frontend_colors.py fails because commit faa1715 added literal hex strings (#991b1b, #fee2e2, #3730a3) to TerminalSimulator.tsx and styles.css. Convert those to rgb(...) tokens in tokens.json and resolve the cargo clippy -- -D warnings lints.
“Every core engine in Axiom NHI—Cedar v4, sqlparser AST, PostgreSQL recursive CTEs, OpenBao leases, and SpiceDB—already exists in the monorepo; production readiness now depends on wiring them into AdminApiState and closing the local-dev shortcuts.”

14-Day Sequenced Remediation Plan to Final Production

Because the underlying Rust crates and Next.js routes are already written, you do not need a multi-month rewrite. Executing the four sequenced engineering sprints below over 14 days resolves all 10 P0–P2 gaps and brings CI, Docker Compose, Helm, and the Cloud Control Plane to production parity.

Sprint 1 (Days 1–3): Green CI & Admin Hardening

Start by making phase1-frontend-gates.yml 100% green: move the hex colors added in commit faa1715 out of TerminalSimulator.tsx into tokens.json, fix all cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings diagnostics, and strip the unconditional axm_local_dev_token_for_browser_testing bypass and allow_origin(Any) from admin.rs.

Sprint 2 (Days 4–7): Wire Postgres, OpenBao & Risk

Retain the PostgresLineageGraph instance inside AdminApiState in main.rs, embed 0002_tenant_rls.sql with FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY into run_migrations(), and wire /v1/lineage/*, /v1/secretless/*, and /v1/owasp/scorecard to call PostgresLineageGraph, OpenBaoClient, and RiskEngine instead of returning static JSON literals.

Sprint 3 (Days 8–14): Cloud Proxy, Auth & Docker

Replace all client-side http://127.0.0.1:8787 fetches in app/console/page.tsx with Next.js server proxy routes (/api/console/*), migrate apps/web/app/api/auth/store.ts from local disk JSON to PostgreSQL with signed JWE cookies in middleware.ts, wire DATABASE_URL and OPENBAO_ADDR in docker-compose.yml, and remove Problems.md from the public root.
